newsitem.title: UK: Freight market up as Panamax rates jump sharply.
newsitem.headline: Freight market up as Panamax rates jump sharply.

text.p: Charterers with November Caper and Panamax cargoes to cover face a rapidly escalating freight market, brokers said.
Panamax levels in particular have jumped significantly further this week, notably for grain and fertilizer shipments in the Atlantic and for coal in the Pacific.

Brokers also now speak of stronger demand in the Indian Ocean area although South America remains relatively weak. A sure sign of firmer market conditions was the emergence of more chartering interest for short period business, especially in the west.

Forecasts of shrinking availability of Capers are also being fulfilled -- Daiichi, for example, were obliged to pay close to $17,000 daily for Sanko Oasis 161,000 dwt delivery continent early Dec for a trip via Narvik to China. The BFI rose 25 points to 1358, a level not seen since the end of May, and brokers are confident the trend will continue this week.

Capers again feated in the grain trades following Romak's fixture on on Monday of Regina 4,175,000 cft Mississippi/Egypt for mid Nov at $1.1m. The 1977-built Finix 123,125 dwt was continued by Dreyfus basis Rotterdam next weekend for a round trip via Port Cartier or US Gulf at $10,000 daily.

There were reports of a 1973-built 120,000 dwt vessel fixing grain from the continent to Iran on subjects at a similar level. Egyptian charterers are said to be pushing hard for Panamaxes from northern France to Egypt. The 1977-built Ipanema 75,203 dwt was rumoured fixed by Bluedeck delivery US Gulf mid Nov trip via Egypt redelivery Passero at $9,000 daily plus $200,000 bonus.

Dreyfus have fixed the 1972-built Pioneer-relet Magnum 68,326 dwt on subjects delivery prompt US Gulf trip Far East at a remarkable $11,850 daily plus $250,000 bonus. Almost as striking was Cho Yang's fixture of the 1980-built Kingston-relet Elli B 61,632 dwt delivery Nov 11/21 for the same trip at $12,000 daily plus $250,000 bonus.

But the Mo Modern tonnage is now commanding around $14,000 daily or more -- the Shinwa-relet National Prosperity 75,100 dwt is understood fixed delivery Ghent mid Nov at $13,800 daily and Konstantinos a 71,550 dwt retro passing Passero at $14,400 daily, both for trips via US Gulf to the Far East. New enquiries on Tuesday included Cargill with 2.7-3.2m cft up river and Brazil/Continent for Nov 25/Dec 5 and Central States 50,000 hss US Gulf/China for Nov 15/28.

In the East Toepfer have not yet fixed their Pananax cargo Nopac/Saudi Arabia with Nov 20 cancelling -- some brokers estimate this business, recently fixed at $16.00/$17.00, could now go for over $20.00. The charterers of Atlantic Sovereign 65,000 dwt open Japan Nov 10/15 failed to lift subjects in time (believed to be for grain Nopac/Bin Qasim) and the vessel is now said to be asking $14,000 daily for any eastern business.

Handy news was thin and conditions are not encouraging for these sizes anywhere except for certain types in the US Gulf. Bunge are believed to be close to fixing 17/20000 hss US Gulf/Vera Cruz for Nov 9/16. On Tuesday Toepfer quoted 1.5/1.7m cft Mississippi/Continent for mid Nov and Cargill have a similar enquiry. Toepfer also now have 15,000 bagged barley Antwerp/Benghazi for prompt shipment. Glencore quote 20,000/5 hss NSW or Victoria/China for Nov 25 onwards.

The market has become firmer for Capers as well as Panamaxes. The 1981-built Thalassini Avra 129,237 dwt is understood fixed delivery Dunkirk second half Nov for a Transatlantic round at $10,500 daily. Frapaco have been linked with the 1977-built Pamphilos 64,100 dwt delivery Gibraltar for a Transatlantic round via Black Sea redelivery Passero at just below $9,000 daily. HMM are believed to have booked Maritime Mosaic 73,657 dwt for coal from Dalrymple to Hong Kong at $7.50. Cargill have fixed 55,000 phosphate Tampa/China for prompt shipment on subjects.
